title: Mini Bio of Katherine Mun
text:
I am a New Yorker who grew up in Flushing, New York, although born in Lawton, Oklahoma.
At Baruch College, I studied accounting and taxation.
My education there has assisted me to succeed as an auditor in the government sector.
Currently, I work for the internal audit department of a New York City agency.
As a Baruch graduate student, I plan to advance my career with a master’s in data analytics.
Meanwhile, I will continue enjoying my religious activities like praying.
I wish you the best at Baruch College!

title: Netflix
text:
#  This function will acquire and standardize all data of "What We Watched Reports"
#  from Netflix. Because Netflix hosts the data files behind a CDN, we
#  are accessing the release pages and automatically extracting links to the
#  relevant files (with CDN hash). 
# 
#  After import, files are stacked vertically and some basic cleaning is
#  performed. 
load_netflix_data <- function(){
  
  library(tidyverse)
  library(rvest)
  library(readxl)
  library(fs)
  library(scales)
  library(gt)

  
  data_dir <- path("data", "mp01")
    
  if(!dir_exists(data_dir)){
    dir_create(data_dir, showWarnings=FALSE, recurse=TRUE)
  }
  
  NETFLIX_URLS <- list(
    `2023H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-a-netflix-engagement-report",
    `2023H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2023",
    `2024H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2024",
    `2024H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2024",
    `2025H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2025",
    `2025H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2025",
    `2026H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2026"
  )
  
  download_if_needed <- function(url, local){
    if(!file_exists(local)){
      download.file(url, local, quiet = TRUE, mode = "wb")
    }
    
    return(local)
  }
    
  NETFLIX_URLS |> 
    map(read_html) |> 
    map(html_element, xpath = "//a[contains(@href, '.xlsx')]") |> 
    map_chr(html_attr, "href") |> 
    enframe("period", "url") |> 
   mutate(path = path(data_dir, paste0(period, ".xlsx")), 
          path = map2(url, path, download_if_needed), 
          data = map(path, read_excel, skip=3, na="*"), 
          data = map(data, \(x) x |> mutate(`Release Date` = as.Date(`Release Date`)))) |>
    unnest(data) |> 
    select(-url, -path) |> 
    mutate(year=str_sub(period, 1, 4), 
           half=str_sub(period, start=6), 
           period_start = make_date(year, if_else(half==1, 1, 7), 1), 
           period_end = make_date(year, if_else(half==1, 6, 12), if_else(half==1, 30, 31))) |> 
    filter(!is.na(`Hours Viewed`)) |> 
    mutate(live_event = !is.na(Runtime) & str_detect(Runtime, "\\d+:\\d+\\*"), 
           clean_time = str_remove(Runtime, fixed("*")),
           Runtime = 60 * hour(hm(clean_time)) + minute(hm(clean_time))) |>
    select(-clean_time) |>
    mutate(Runtime = coalesce(Runtime, mean(Runtime, na.rm=TRUE)), 
           .by=Title, 
           Title = stringi::stri_trans_general(Title, "Latin-ASCII"),
           Title = str_remove(Title, " // .*"), 
           Title = str_remove(Title, "[^[:ascii:]].*"), 
           Title = str_trim(Title)) |>
    filter_out(Title == "") |>
    select(year, 
           period, 
           period_start, 
           period_end, 
           Title, 
           -half, 
           Runtime, 
           Views, 
           `Hours Viewed`, 
           `Release Date`,
           `Available Globally?`, 
           live_event)
    }

  NETFLIX_DATA <- load_netflix_data()

  NETFLIX_DATA1 <- NETFLIX_DATA |>
    rename(title = Title,

           views = Views,

          available_globally = as.logical("Yes" == TRUE, "No" == FALSE))

# Create a table listing top titles by the number of views and fraction of hours viewed for each period. The total of   views in each period was used to show the top title's percentage of views. 

Top_Title <- NETFLIX_DATA1 |>
  group_by(period) |>
  summarize(totalviews = sum(views, na.rm = TRUE),
            highest_viewhours = max(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE))

Top_Title1 <- NETFLIX_DATA1 |>
  select(period, title, hours_viewed, views) |>
  inner_join(Top_Title, by = c("hours_viewed" = "highest_viewhours"))|>
  select(-period.y)|>
  rename(period = period.x)|>
  mutate(percent_views = percent(hours_viewed/totalviews))

# Create a table showing the titles with most consistently high viewership across all periods. To find the titles      appearing in all periods, the number of counts equaling seven was filtered. 

Viewership <- NETFLIX_DATA1 |>
  count(title)|>
  filter(n == 7)

# For each titles appearing in all seven periods, the total of views with the standard deviation, average, and the     minimum were calculated. The results were sorted by ascending order of standard deviation and descending order of    average views to show the most consistently viewed titles. 

Viewership1 <- NETFLIX_DATA1 |>
  select(title, views) |>
  inner_join(Viewership, by = c("title" = "title"))|>
  group_by(title) |>
  summarize(totalviews = sum(views, na.rm = TRUE),
            std_dev_views = sd(views, na.rm = TRUE),
            avg_views = mean(views, na.rm = TRUE),
            minimum_views = min(views, na.rm = FALSE))|>
  arrange(desc(avg_views), na.rm = FALSE)|>
  arrange(std_dev_views, na.rm = FALSE)              
  
gt(Viewership1)|>
  tab_header(title = "Most Consistently Viewed Titles in Every Seven Months, 2023H1 to 2026H1",  
             subtitle = "by ascending order of standard deviation and descending order 
                         of average of views")

# Create a table showing estimated fractions of shows and movies viewed in each period.

# Runtime in each half of calendar year was divided by 26 weeks to find whether the result was more than four          hours per week, likely indicating the title was a show. Furthermore, any title with "Season" was counted as a show.     
Show <- NETFLIX_DATA1|>
  filter(runtime/26 > 4 | str_detect(title, "Season"))|>
  group_by(period)|>
  summarize(total_shows = length(unique(title)),
            show_hoursviewed = sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE))

# Titles with less than or equal to four hours of runtime in every week of half calendar year, but excluding those     with "Season," likely indicates the title was a movie.

Movie <- NETFLIX_DATA1|>
  filter(runtime/26 <= 4 | is.na(runtime))|>
  filter_out(str_detect(title, "Season"))|>
  group_by(period)|>
  summarize(total_movies = length(unique(title)),
            movie_hoursviewed = sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE))

# For each period, the total of hours viewed with the percentages of views for shows and movies were calculated. 

Timespent <- Show|>
  inner_join(Movie, by = "period")|>
  mutate(total_hoursviewed = show_hoursviewed + movie_hoursviewed,
            percent_shows_hoursviewed = percent(show_hoursviewed/total_hoursviewed, accuracy = 0.01),
            percent_movies_hoursviewed = percent(movie_hoursviewed/total_hoursviewed, accuracy = 0.01))|>
  select(-total_hoursviewed)

gt(Timespent)|>
     tab_header(title = "Estimated Fractions Spent on Watching Shows and Movies",
                subtitle = "2023H1 to 2026H1")

Title: Netflix Corporate Strategy Memo for 2027
To: Management
From: Katherine Mun
Date: October 16, 2026

Executive Summary
The number of views and view hours for 24,427 titles that ran in a half calendar year, between  2023-01-01 and 2026-06-30, were analyzed to plan releases in 2027.
Findings of Analysis
Between second half of 2024 and first half of 2026, around 98% or 99% of the total views came from pre-taped contents in each six months because of a high number of pre-taped contents. Approximately 7,000 and 8,000 were pre-taped contents, while less than 120 were live events.

Among the pre-taped contents, approximately 71% of shows and 29% of movies were viewed in the first half of 2023. However, since the second half of 2023, approximately 97% to 99% of shows were viewed because of a high number of shows. Approximately 6,000 to 7,500 were shows, while the number of movies has decreased from approximately 11,000 to below 700.
Recommendation
Based on the analysis, Netflix should continue to run a high number of pre-taped shows in 2027 to increase viewership.

library(tidyverse)

## ✖ dplyr::filter() masks stats::filter()
## ✖ dplyr::lag()    masks stats::lag()
## ℹ Use the conflicted package (<http://conflicted.r-lib.org/>) to force all conflicts to become errors
library(stringr)
library(httr2)
library(rvest)
## 
## Attaching package: 'rvest'
## 
## The following object is masked from 'package:readr':
## 
##     guess_encoding

get_eia_sep <- function(state, abbr){
    library(tidyverse)
    library(stringr)
    library(httr2)
    library(rvest)
    library(fs)
  
    state_formatted <- str_to_lower(state) |> str_replace_all("\\s", "")
    
    dir_name <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
    file_name <- fs::path(dir_name, state_formatted)
    
    fs::dir_create(dir_name, recurse=TRUE)
    
    if(!fs::file_exists(file_name)){
        BASE_URL <- "https://www.eia.gov"
        RESPONSE <- request(BASE_URL) |> 
          req_url_path("electricity", 
                       "state", 
                       state_formatted) |>
          req_headers(
            `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0"
            ) |>   
          req_retry(
                max_tries = 4, 
          ) |>
          req_perform(file_name)
    
        resp_check_status(RESPONSE)
    }
    
    TABLE <- read_html(file_name) |> 
        html_element("table") |> 
        html_table() |>
        mutate(Item = str_to_lower(Item))
    
    if("U.S. rank" %in% colnames(TABLE)){
        TABLE <- TABLE |> rename(Rank = `U.S. rank`)
    }
    
    CO2_MWh <- TABLE |> 
        filter(Item == "carbon dioxide (lbs/mwh)") |>
        pull(Value) |> 
        str_replace_all(",", "") |>
        as.numeric()
    
    PRIMARY <- TABLE |> 
        filter(Item == "primary energy source") |> 
        pull(Rank)
    
    RATE <- TABLE |>
        filter(Item == "average retail price (cents/kwh)") |>
        pull(Value) |>
        as.numeric()
    
    GENERATION_MWh <- TABLE |>
        filter(Item == "net generation (megawatthours)") |>
        pull(Value) |>
        str_replace_all(",", "") |>
        as.numeric()
    
    data.frame(CO2_MWh               = CO2_MWh, 
               primary_source        = PRIMARY,
               electricity_price_MWh = RATE * 10, # / 100 cents to dollars &
               # * 1000 kWh to MWH 
               generation_MWh        = GENERATION_MWh, 
               state                 = state, 
               abbreviation          = abbr
    )
}

EIA_SEP_REPORT <- map2(state.name, state.abb, get_eia_sep) |> list_rbind()

load_ntd_energy <- function(){
  library(readxl)
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  
  # Create 'data/mp02' directory if not already present
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)

  NTD_ENERGY_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_energy.xlsx")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
  
    request("https://www.transit.dot.gov/") |>
      req_url_path("sites",
                   "fta.dot.gov",
                   "files",
                   "2026-09",
                   "2025 Energy Consumption_260806.xlsx") |> 
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)$size < 1e4){
        cat("I was unable to download the NTD Energy File. Please try again.\n")
        stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_energy.xlsx')` and try again.")
    }

  to_numeric_fill_0 <- function(x){
    x <- if_else(x == "-", NA, x)
    replace_na(as.numeric(x), 0)
  }

  read_excel(NTD_ENERGY_FILE) |> 
    select(-c(`Reporter Type`, 
              `Reporting Module`, 
              `Gallons of Other Fuel`, 
              `Other Fuel Description`)) |>
    mutate(across(-c(`Agency Name`, 
                     `Mode`,
                     `TOS`), 
                  to_numeric_fill_0)) |>
    group_by(`NTD ID`, `Mode`, `Agency Name`) |>
    summarize(across(where(is.numeric), sum), 
              .groups = "keep") |>
    mutate(ENERGY = sum(c_across(c(where(is.numeric))))) |>
    filter(ENERGY > 0) |>
    select(-ENERGY) |>
    ungroup()
}

NTD_ENERGY <- load_ntd_energy()

load_ntd_service <- function(){
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  
  # Create 'data/mp02' directory if not already present
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)

  NTD_SERVICE_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_service.csv")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
  
    request("https://data.transportation.gov/resource/4fir-qbim.csv") |>
      req_url_query(`$query`=paste(
        "SELECT  `_5_digit_ntd_id` AS `NTD_ID`", 
        "`max_agency` AS `AGENCY`",
        "`max_reporter_type` AS `reporter_type`",
        "`max_organization_type` AS `organization_type`",
        "`max_city` AS `city`",
        "`max_state` AS `state`",
        "`mode`",
        "`type_of_service`",
        "`max_primary_uza_code` as `uza_code`",
        "`max_primary_uza_name` as `uza_name`",
        "`max_primary_uza_area_sq_miles` as `uza_sq_miles`",
        "`max_primary_uza_population` as `uza_population`",
        "`max_service_area_sq_miles` as `service_area_sq_miles`",
        "`max_service_area_population` as `service_area_population`",
        "`questionable_record` as `flagged_likely_inaccurate`",
        "`sum_unlinked_passenger_trips_upt` as `total_upt`",
        "`sum_passenger_miles` WHERE caseless_one_of(`report_year`, '2025') limit 50000", 
        sep=",")) |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)$size < 1e4){
        cat("I was unable to download the NTD Service File. Please try again.\n")
        stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_service.xlsx')` and try again.")
    }

  read_csv(NTD_SERVICE_FILE) |>
    mutate(flagged_likely_inaccurate = !is.na(flagged_likely_inaccurate))
}

NTD_ENERGY <- NTD_ENERGY |>  
  mutate(n_distinct(Mode),

# Delete leading zeros in the agency IDs and select columns.
NTD_SERVICE1 <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  mutate(`NTD ID` = as.numeric(NTD_ID)) |>
  select(`AGENCY`, `state`, `NTD ID`) |>
  distinct()

# Join data sets and select columns.
Emission_1 <- inner_join(NTD_SERVICE1, NTD_ENERGY, by = "NTD ID") |>
  select(`AGENCY`, `Mode`, `state`, starts_with("Gallons of"))

# Select columns and rename the column of abbreviated states.

  select(`abbreviation`, CO2_MWh) |>
  rename("state" = "abbreviation")

# Join data sets and delete columns with only zeros for gallons of fuel.
Total_Emission <- inner_join(Emission_1, Emission_2, by = "state") |>
  select(where(~ !is.numeric(.) | sum(. != 0, na.rm = TRUE) > 0)) |>
  
# Use gallons per pound of carbon dioxide based on the EIA and EPA websites. 
  mutate(CO2_totalemission_lbs = `Gallons of Bio-Diesel` * 20.83 +
                                 `Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas` * 14.83 +
                                 `Gallons of Diesel Fuel` * 22.45 +
                                 `Gallons of Ethanol` * 12.68 +
                                 `Gallons of Gasoline` * 20.86 +
                                 `Gallons of Liquified Nat Gas` * 9.92 +
                                 `Gallons of Liquified Petroleum Gas` * 12.52)

# Select columns and rename one. 
  select(1:3, 8, 9) |>

# Join data sets to calculate each agency's emission per UPT and passenger mile.
Transit_Usage <- inner_join(Total_Emission, NTD_SERVICE2, 
                            by = c("AGENCY", "Mode", "state")) |>
  select(1, 12:14)|>
  group_by(`AGENCY`) |>
  summarize(across(where(is.numeric), ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE))) |>
  mutate(CO2emission_per_upt = CO2_totalemission_lbs / total_upt,
         CO2emission_per_passengermile = CO2_totalemission_lbs / sum_passenger_miles)

# Find the agency most efficient in carbon dioxide emission per UPT.
Efficient_UPT <- Transit_Usage |>
  filter(CO2_totalemission_lbs > 0) |>
  slice_min(CO2emission_per_upt, n = 1) |>

Figure_UPT <- Transit_Usage |>

  slice_min(CO2emission_per_upt, n = 1) |>

# Find the agency most efficient in carbon dioxide emission per passenger mile.
Efficient_Mile <- Transit_Usage |>
  filter(CO2_totalemission_lbs > 0) |>
  slice_min(CO2emission_per_passengermile, n = 1) |>

# Find the figure of the agency's carbon dioxide emission per passenger mile.
Figure_Mile <- Transit_Usage |>

#  This function will acquire and standardize all data of "What We Watched Reports"
#  from Netflix. Because Netflix hosts the data files behind a CDN, we
#  are accessing the release pages and automatically extracting links to the
#  relevant files (with CDN hash). 
# 
#  After import, files are stacked vertically and some basic cleaning is
#  performed. 
load_netflix_data <- function(){
  
  library(tidyverse)
  library(rvest)
  library(readxl)
  library(fs)
  library(scales)
  library(gt)

  
  data_dir <- path("data", "mp01")
    
  if(!dir_exists(data_dir)){
    dir_create(data_dir, showWarnings=FALSE, recurse=TRUE)
  }
  
  NETFLIX_URLS <- list(
    `2023H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-a-netflix-engagement-report",
    `2023H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2023",
    `2024H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2024",
    `2024H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2024",
    `2025H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2025",
    `2025H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2025",
    `2026H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2026"
  )
  
  download_if_needed <- function(url, local){
    if(!file_exists(local)){
      download.file(url, local, quiet = TRUE, mode = "wb")
    }
    
    return(local)
  }
    
  NETFLIX_URLS |> 
    map(read_html) |> 
    map(html_element, xpath = "//a[contains(@href, '.xlsx')]") |> 
    map_chr(html_attr, "href") |> 
    enframe("period", "url") |> 
   mutate(path = path(data_dir, paste0(period, ".xlsx")), 
          path = map2(url, path, download_if_needed), 
          data = map(path, read_excel, skip=3, na="*"), 
          data = map(data, \(x) x |> mutate(`Release Date` = as.Date(`Release Date`)))) |>
    unnest(data) |> 
    select(-url, -path) |> 
    mutate(year=str_sub(period, 1, 4), 
           half=str_sub(period, start=6), 
           period_start = make_date(year, if_else(half==1, 1, 7), 1), 
           period_end = make_date(year, if_else(half==1, 6, 12), if_else(half==1, 30, 31))) |> 
    filter(!is.na(`Hours Viewed`)) |> 
    mutate(live_event = !is.na(Runtime) & str_detect(Runtime, "\\d+:\\d+\\*"), 
           clean_time = str_remove(Runtime, fixed("*")),
           Runtime = 60 * hour(hm(clean_time)) + minute(hm(clean_time))) |>
    select(-clean_time) |>
    mutate(Runtime = coalesce(Runtime, mean(Runtime, na.rm=TRUE)), 
           .by=Title, 
           Title = stringi::stri_trans_general(Title, "Latin-ASCII"),
           Title = str_remove(Title, " // .*"), 
           Title = str_remove(Title, "[^[:ascii:]].*"), 
           Title = str_trim(Title)) |>
    filter_out(Title == "") |>
    select(year, 
           period, 
           period_start, 
           period_end, 
           Title, 
           -half, 
           Runtime, 
           Views, 
           `Hours Viewed`, 
           `Release Date`,
           `Available Globally?`, 
           live_event)
    }

  NETFLIX_DATA <- load_netflix_data()

# Create a table showing estimated fractions of shows and movies viewed in each period.

# Runtime in each half of calendar year was divided by 26 weeks to find whether the result was more than four          hours per week, likely indicating the title was a show. Furthermore, any title with "Season" was counted as a show.     
Show <- NETFLIX_DATA1|>
  filter(runtime/26 > 4 | str_detect(title, "Season"))|>
  group_by(period)|>
  summarize(total_shows = length(unique(title)),
            show_hoursviewed = sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE))

# Titles with less than or equal to four hours of runtime in every week of half calendar year, but excluding those     with "Season," likely indicates the title was a movie.

Movie <- NETFLIX_DATA1|>
  filter(runtime/26 <= 4 | is.na(runtime))|>
  filter_out(str_detect(title, "Season"))|>
  group_by(period)|>
  summarize(total_movies = length(unique(title)),
            movie_hoursviewed = sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE))

# For each period, the total of hours viewed with the percentages of views for shows and movies were calculated. 

Timespent <- Show|>
  inner_join(Movie, by = "period")|>
  mutate(total_hoursviewed = show_hoursviewed + movie_hoursviewed,
            percent_shows_hoursviewed = percent(show_hoursviewed/total_hoursviewed, accuracy = 0.01),
            percent_movies_hoursviewed = percent(movie_hoursviewed/total_hoursviewed, accuracy = 0.01))|>
  select(-total_hoursviewed)

Title: Netflix Corporate Strategy Memo for 2027
To: Management
From: Katherine Mun
Date: October 16, 2026

Executive Summary
The number of views and view hours for 24,427 titles that ran in a half calendar year, between  2023-01-01 and 2026-06-30, were analyzed to plan releases in 2027.
Findings of Analysis
Between second half of 2024 and first half of 2026, around 98% or 99% of the total views came from pre-taped contents in each six months because of a high number of pre-taped contents. Approximately 7,000 and 8,000 were pre-taped contents, while less than 120 were live events.

Among the pre-taped contents, approximately 71% of shows and 29% of movies were viewed in the first half of 2023. However, since the second half of 2023, approximately 97% to 99% of shows were viewed because of a high number of shows. Approximately 6,000 to 7,500 were shows, while the number of movies has decreased from approximately 11,000 to below 700.
Recommendation
Based on the analysis, Netflix should continue to run a high number of pre-taped shows in 2027 to increase viewership.






NoteAI Usage Statement





I did not use Generative AI tools to complete this mini-project.

#  This function will acquire and standardize all data of "What We Watched Reports"
#  from Netflix. Because Netflix hosts the data files behind a CDN, we
#  are accessing the release pages and automatically extracting links to the
#  relevant files (with CDN hash). 
# 
#  After import, files are stacked vertically and some basic cleaning is
#  performed. 
load_netflix_data <- function(){
  
  library(tidyverse)
  library(rvest)
  library(readxl)
  library(fs)
  library(scales)
  library(gt)

  
  data_dir <- path("data", "mp01")
    
  if(!dir_exists(data_dir)){
    dir_create(data_dir, showWarnings=FALSE, recurse=TRUE)
  }
  
  NETFLIX_URLS <- list(
    `2023H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-a-netflix-engagement-report",
    `2023H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2023",
    `2024H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2024",
    `2024H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2024",
    `2025H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2025",
    `2025H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2025",
    `2026H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2026"
  )
  
  download_if_needed <- function(url, local){
    if(!file_exists(local)){
      download.file(url, local, quiet = TRUE, mode = "wb")
    }
    
    return(local)
  }
    
  NETFLIX_URLS |> 
    map(read_html) |> 
    map(html_element, xpath = "//a[contains(@href, '.xlsx')]") |> 
    map_chr(html_attr, "href") |> 
    enframe("period", "url") |> 
   mutate(path = path(data_dir, paste0(period, ".xlsx")), 
          path = map2(url, path, download_if_needed), 
          data = map(path, read_excel, skip=3, na="*"), 
          data = map(data, \(x) x |> mutate(`Release Date` = as.Date(`Release Date`)))) |>
    unnest(data) |> 
    select(-url, -path) |> 
    mutate(year=str_sub(period, 1, 4), 
           half=str_sub(period, start=6), 
           period_start = make_date(year, if_else(half==1, 1, 7), 1), 
           period_end = make_date(year, if_else(half==1, 6, 12), if_else(half==1, 30, 31))) |> 
    filter(!is.na(`Hours Viewed`)) |> 
    mutate(live_event = !is.na(Runtime) & str_detect(Runtime, "\\d+:\\d+\\*"), 
           clean_time = str_remove(Runtime, fixed("*")),
           Runtime = 60 * hour(hm(clean_time)) + minute(hm(clean_time))) |>
    select(-clean_time) |>
    mutate(Runtime = coalesce(Runtime, mean(Runtime, na.rm=TRUE)), 
           .by=Title, 
           Title = stringi::stri_trans_general(Title, "Latin-ASCII"),
           Title = str_remove(Title, " // .*"), 
           Title = str_remove(Title, "[^[:ascii:]].*"), 
           Title = str_trim(Title)) |>
    filter_out(Title == "") |>
    select(year, 
           period, 
           period_start, 
           period_end, 
           Title, 
           -half, 
           Runtime, 
           Views, 
           `Hours Viewed`, 
           `Release Date`,
           `Available Globally?`, 
           live_event)
    }

  NETFLIX_DATA <- load_netflix_data()

# Create a table showing estimated fractions of shows and movies viewed in each period.

# Runtime in each half of calendar year was divided by 26 weeks to find whether the result was more than four          hours per week, likely indicating the title was a show. Furthermore, any title with "Season" was counted as a show.     
Show <- NETFLIX_DATA1|>
  filter(runtime/26 > 4 | str_detect(title, "Season"))|>
  group_by(period)|>
  summarize(total_shows = length(unique(title)),
            show_hoursviewed = sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE))

# Titles with less than or equal to four hours of runtime in every week of half calendar year, but excluding those     with "Season," likely indicates the title was a movie.

Movie <- NETFLIX_DATA1|>
  filter(runtime/26 <= 4 | is.na(runtime))|>
  filter_out(str_detect(title, "Season"))|>
  group_by(period)|>
  summarize(total_movies = length(unique(title)),
            movie_hoursviewed = sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE))

# For each period, the total of hours viewed with the percentages of views for shows and movies were calculated. 

Timespent <- Show|>
  inner_join(Movie, by = "period")|>
  mutate(total_hoursviewed = show_hoursviewed + movie_hoursviewed,
            percent_shows_hoursviewed = percent(show_hoursviewed/total_hoursviewed, accuracy = 0.01),
            percent_movies_hoursviewed = percent(movie_hoursviewed/total_hoursviewed, accuracy = 0.01))|>
  select(-total_hoursviewed)

gt(Timespent)|>
     tab_header(title = "Estimated Fractions Spent on Watching Shows and Movies",
                subtitle = "2023H1 to 2026H1")

Live <- NETFLIX_DATA1 |>

  full_join(Live, by = "period")|>
  mutate(totalviews = taped_content_views + live_event_views,
         avg.views_taped_contents = percent(taped_content_views/totalviews, accuracy = 0.01),
         avg.views_live_event = percent(live_event_views/totalviews, accuracy = 0.01))|>

#  This function will acquire and standardize all data of "What We Watched Reports"
#  from Netflix. Because Netflix hosts the data files behind a CDN, we
#  are accessing the release pages and automatically extracting links to the
#  relevant files (with CDN hash). 
# 
#  After import, files are stacked vertically and some basic cleaning is
#  performed. 
load_netflix_data <- function(){
  
  library(tidyverse)
  library(rvest)
  library(readxl)
  library(fs)
  library(scales)
  library(gt)

  
  data_dir <- path("data", "mp01")
    
  if(!dir_exists(data_dir)){
    dir_create(data_dir, showWarnings=FALSE, recurse=TRUE)
  }
  
  NETFLIX_URLS <- list(
    `2023H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-a-netflix-engagement-report",
    `2023H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2023",
    `2024H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2024",
    `2024H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2024",
    `2025H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2025",
    `2025H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2025",
    `2026H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2026"
  )
  
  download_if_needed <- function(url, local){
    if(!file_exists(local)){
      download.file(url, local, quiet = TRUE, mode = "wb")
    }
    
    return(local)
  }
    
  NETFLIX_URLS |> 
    map(read_html) |> 
    map(html_element, xpath = "//a[contains(@href, '.xlsx')]") |> 
    map_chr(html_attr, "href") |> 
    enframe("period", "url") |> 
   mutate(path = path(data_dir, paste0(period, ".xlsx")), 
          path = map2(url, path, download_if_needed), 
          data = map(path, read_excel, skip=3, na="*"), 
          data = map(data, \(x) x |> mutate(`Release Date` = as.Date(`Release Date`)))) |>
    unnest(data) |> 
    select(-url, -path) |> 
    mutate(year=str_sub(period, 1, 4), 
           half=str_sub(period, start=6), 
           period_start = make_date(year, if_else(half==1, 1, 7), 1), 
           period_end = make_date(year, if_else(half==1, 6, 12), if_else(half==1, 30, 31))) |> 
    filter(!is.na(`Hours Viewed`)) |> 
    mutate(live_event = !is.na(Runtime) & str_detect(Runtime, "\\d+:\\d+\\*"), 
           clean_time = str_remove(Runtime, fixed("*")),
           Runtime = 60 * hour(hm(clean_time)) + minute(hm(clean_time))) |>
    select(-clean_time) |>
    mutate(Runtime = coalesce(Runtime, mean(Runtime, na.rm=TRUE)), 
           .by=Title, 
           Title = stringi::stri_trans_general(Title, "Latin-ASCII"),
           Title = str_remove(Title, " // .*"), 
           Title = str_remove(Title, "[^[:ascii:]].*"), 
           Title = str_trim(Title)) |>
    filter_out(Title == "") |>
    select(year, 
           period, 
           period_start, 
           period_end, 
           Title, 
           -half, 
           Runtime, 
           Views, 
           `Hours Viewed`, 
           `Release Date`,
           `Available Globally?`, 
           live_event)
    }

# Create a table showing estimated fractions of shows and movies viewed in each period.

# Runtime in each half of calendar year was divided by 26 weeks to find whether the result was more than four          hours per week, likely indicating the title was a show. Furthermore, any title with "Season" was counted as a show.     
Show <- NETFLIX_DATA1|>
  filter(runtime/26 > 4 | str_detect(title, "Season"))|>
  group_by(period)|>
  summarize(total_shows = length(unique(title)),
            show_hoursviewed = sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE))

# Titles with less than or equal to four hours of runtime in every week of half calendar year, but excluding those     with "Season," likely indicates the title was a movie.

Movie <- NETFLIX_DATA1|>
  filter(runtime/26 <= 4 | is.na(runtime))|>
  filter_out(str_detect(title, "Season"))|>
  group_by(period)|>
  summarize(total_movies = length(unique(title)),
            movie_hoursviewed = sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE))

# For each period, the total of hours viewed with the percentages of views for shows and movies were calculated. 

Timespent <- Show|>
  inner_join(Movie, by = "period")|>
  mutate(total_hoursviewed = show_hoursviewed + movie_hoursviewed,
            percent_shows_hoursviewed = percent(show_hoursviewed/total_hoursviewed, accuracy = 0.01),
            percent_movies_hoursviewed = percent(movie_hoursviewed/total_hoursviewed, accuracy = 0.01))|>
  select(-total_hoursviewed)

gt(Timespent)|>
     tab_header(title = "Estimated Fractions Spent on Watching Shows and Movies",
                subtitle = "2023H1 to 2026H1")

Title: Netflix Corporate Strategy Memo for 2027
To: Management
From: Katherine Mun
Date: October 16, 2026

Executive Summary
The number of views and view hours for 24,427 titles that ran in a half calendar year, between  2023-01-01 and 2026-06-30, were analyzed to plan releases in 2027.
Findings of Analysis
Between second half of 2024 and first half of 2026, around 98% or 99% of the total views came from pre-taped contents in each six months because of a high number of pre-taped contents. Approximately 7,000 and 8,000 were pre-taped contents, while less than 120 were live events.

Among the pre-taped contents, approximately 71% of shows and 29% of movies were viewed in the first half of 2023. However, since the second half of 2023, approximately 97% to 99% of shows were viewed because of a high number of shows. Approximately 6,000 to 7,500 were shows, while the number of movies has decreased from approximately 11,000 to below 700.
Recommendation
Based on the analysis, Netflix should continue to run a high number of pre-taped shows in 2027 to increase viewership.

#  This function will acquire and standardize all data of "What We Watched Reports"
#  from Netflix. Because Netflix hosts the data files behind a CDN, we
#  are accessing the release pages and automatically extracting links to the
#  relevant files (with CDN hash). 
# 
#  After import, files are stacked vertically and some basic cleaning is
#  performed. 
load_netflix_data <- function(){
  
  library(tidyverse)
  library(rvest)
  library(readxl)
  library(fs)
  library(scales)
  library(gt)

  
  data_dir <- path("data", "mp01")
    
  if(!dir_exists(data_dir)){
    dir_create(data_dir, showWarnings=FALSE, recurse=TRUE)
  }
  
  NETFLIX_URLS <- list(
    `2023H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-a-netflix-engagement-report",
    `2023H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2023",
    `2024H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2024",
    `2024H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2024",
    `2025H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2025",
    `2025H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2025",
    `2026H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2026"
  )
  
  download_if_needed <- function(url, local){
    if(!file_exists(local)){
      download.file(url, local, quiet = TRUE, mode = "wb")
    }
    
    return(local)
  }
    
  NETFLIX_URLS |> 
    map(read_html) |> 
    map(html_element, xpath = "//a[contains(@href, '.xlsx')]") |> 
    map_chr(html_attr, "href") |> 
    enframe("period", "url") |> 
   mutate(path = path(data_dir, paste0(period, ".xlsx")), 
          path = map2(url, path, download_if_needed), 
          data = map(path, read_excel, skip=3, na="*"), 
          data = map(data, \(x) x |> mutate(`Release Date` = as.Date(`Release Date`)))) |>
    unnest(data) |> 
    select(-url, -path) |> 
    mutate(year=str_sub(period, 1, 4), 
           half=str_sub(period, start=6), 
           period_start = make_date(year, if_else(half==1, 1, 7), 1), 
           period_end = make_date(year, if_else(half==1, 6, 12), if_else(half==1, 30, 31))) |> 
    filter(!is.na(`Hours Viewed`)) |> 
    mutate(live_event = !is.na(Runtime) & str_detect(Runtime, "\\d+:\\d+\\*"), 
           clean_time = str_remove(Runtime, fixed("*")),
           Runtime = 60 * hour(hm(clean_time)) + minute(hm(clean_time))) |>
    select(-clean_time) |>
    mutate(Runtime = coalesce(Runtime, mean(Runtime, na.rm=TRUE)), 
           .by=Title, 
           Title = stringi::stri_trans_general(Title, "Latin-ASCII"),
           Title = str_remove(Title, " // .*"), 
           Title = str_remove(Title, "[^[:ascii:]].*"), 
           Title = str_trim(Title)) |>
    filter_out(Title == "") |>
    select(year, 
           period, 
           period_start, 
           period_end, 
           Title, 
           -half, 
           Runtime, 
           Views, 
           `Hours Viewed`, 
           `Release Date`,
           `Available Globally?`, 
           live_event)
    }

  NETFLIX_DATA <- load_netflix_data()

# Create a table showing changes to the number of titles and runtime in each period based on the previous period.

Change <- NETFLIX_DATA1 |>
  group_by(period) |>
  summarize(total_title = length(unique(title)),
            total_runtime = sum(runtime, na.rm = TRUE))|>
  mutate(percentchange_title = percent((total_title - lag(total_title))/lag(total_title)),
                percentchange_runtime = percent((total_runtime - lag(total_runtime))/lag(total_runtime)))

  gt(Change)|>
     tab_header(title = "Changes in Number of Titles and Runtime From Previous Period", 
                subtitle = "in Each Half of Calendar Year")

# Create a table showing the titles with most consistently high viewership across all periods. To find the titles      appearing in all periods, the number of counts equaling seven was filtered. 

Viewership <- NETFLIX_DATA1 |>
  count(title)|>
  filter(n == 7)

# For each titles appearing in all seven periods, the total of views with the standard deviation, average, and the     minimum were calculated. The results were sorted by ascending order of standard deviation and descending order of    average views to show the most consistently viewed titles. 

Viewership1 <- NETFLIX_DATA1 |>
  select(title, views) |>
  inner_join(Viewership, by = c("title" = "title"))|>
  group_by(title) |>
  summarize(totalviews = sum(views, na.rm = TRUE),
            std_dev_views = sd(views, na.rm = TRUE),
            avg_views = mean(views, na.rm = TRUE),
            minimum_views = min(views, na.rm = FALSE))|>
  arrange(desc(avg_views), na.rm = FALSE)|>
  arrange(std_dev_views, na.rm = FALSE)              
  
gt(Viewership1)|>
  tab_header(title = "Most Consistently Viewed Titles in Every Seven Months, 2023H1 to 2026H1",  
             subtitle = "by ascending order of standard deviation and descending order 
                         of average of views")

# Create a table showing estimated fractions of shows and movies viewed in each period.

# Runtime in each half of calendar year was divided by 26 weeks to find whether the result was more than four          hours per week, likely indicating the title was a show. Furthermore, any title with "Season" was counted as a show.     
Show <- NETFLIX_DATA1|>
  filter(runtime/26 > 4 | str_detect(title, "Season"))|>
  group_by(period)|>
  summarize(total_shows = length(unique(title)),
            show_hoursviewed = sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE))

# Titles with less than or equal to four hours of runtime in every week of half calendar year, but excluding those     with "Season," likely indicates the title was a movie.

Movie <- NETFLIX_DATA1|>
  filter(runtime/26 <= 4 | is.na(runtime))|>
  filter_out(str_detect(title, "Season"))|>
  group_by(period)|>
  summarize(total_movies = length(unique(title)),
            movie_hoursviewed = sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE))

# For each period, the total of hours viewed with the percentages of views for shows and movies were calculated. 

Timespent <- Show|>
  inner_join(Movie, by = "period")|>
  mutate(total_hoursviewed = show_hoursviewed + movie_hoursviewed,
            percent_shows_hoursviewed = percent(show_hoursviewed/total_hoursviewed, accuracy = 0.01),
            percent_movies_hoursviewed = percent(movie_hoursviewed/total_hoursviewed, accuracy = 0.01))|>
  select(-total_hoursviewed)

gt(Timespent)|>
     tab_header(title = "Estimated Fractions Spent on Watching Shows and Movies",
                subtitle = "2023H1 to 2026H1")

Title: Netflix Corporate Strategy Memo for 2027
To: Management
From: Katherine Mun
Date: October 16, 2026

Executive Summary
The number of views and view hours for 24,427 titles that ran in a half calendar year, between  2023-01-01 and 2026-06-30, were analyzed to plan releases in 2027.
Findings of Analysis
Between second half of 2024 and first half of 2026, around 98% or 99% of the total views came from pre-taped contents in each six months because of a high number of pre-taped contents. Approximately 7,000 and 8,000 were pre-taped contents, while less than 120 were live events.

Among the pre-taped contents, approximately 71% of shows and 29% of movies were viewed in the first half of 2023. However, since the second half of 2023, approximately 97% to 99% of shows were viewed because of a high number of shows. Approximately 6,000 to 7,500 were shows, while the number of movies has decreased from approximately 11,000 to below 700.
Recommendation
Based on the analysis, Netflix should continue to run a high number of pre-taped shows in 2027 to increase viewership.

#  This function will acquire and standardize all data of "What We Watched Reports"
#  from Netflix. Because Netflix hosts the data files behind a CDN, we
#  are accessing the release pages and automatically extracting links to the
#  relevant files (with CDN hash). 
# 
#  After import, files are stacked vertically and some basic cleaning is
#  performed. 
load_netflix_data <- function(){
  
  library(tidyverse)
  library(rvest)
  library(readxl)
  library(fs)
  library(scales)
  library(gt)

  
  data_dir <- path("data", "mp01")
    
  if(!dir_exists(data_dir)){
    dir_create(data_dir, showWarnings=FALSE, recurse=TRUE)
  }
  
  NETFLIX_URLS <- list(
    `2023H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-a-netflix-engagement-report",
    `2023H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2023",
    `2024H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2024",
    `2024H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2024",
    `2025H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2025",
    `2025H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2025",
    `2026H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2026"
  )
  
  download_if_needed <- function(url, local){
    if(!file_exists(local)){
      download.file(url, local, quiet = TRUE, mode = "wb")
    }
    
    return(local)
  }
    
  NETFLIX_URLS |> 
    map(read_html) |> 
    map(html_element, xpath = "//a[contains(@href, '.xlsx')]") |> 
    map_chr(html_attr, "href") |> 
    enframe("period", "url") |> 
   mutate(path = path(data_dir, paste0(period, ".xlsx")), 
          path = map2(url, path, download_if_needed), 
          data = map(path, read_excel, skip=3, na="*"), 
          data = map(data, \(x) x |> mutate(`Release Date` = as.Date(`Release Date`)))) |>
    unnest(data) |> 
    select(-url, -path) |> 
    mutate(year=str_sub(period, 1, 4), 
           half=str_sub(period, start=6), 
           period_start = make_date(year, if_else(half==1, 1, 7), 1), 
           period_end = make_date(year, if_else(half==1, 6, 12), if_else(half==1, 30, 31))) |> 
    filter(!is.na(`Hours Viewed`)) |> 
    mutate(live_event = !is.na(Runtime) & str_detect(Runtime, "\\d+:\\d+\\*"), 
           clean_time = str_remove(Runtime, fixed("*")),
           Runtime = 60 * hour(hm(clean_time)) + minute(hm(clean_time))) |>
    select(-clean_time) |>
    mutate(Runtime = coalesce(Runtime, mean(Runtime, na.rm=TRUE)), 
           .by=Title, 
           Title = stringi::stri_trans_general(Title, "Latin-ASCII"),
           Title = str_remove(Title, " // .*"), 
           Title = str_remove(Title, "[^[:ascii:]].*"), 
           Title = str_trim(Title)) |>
    filter_out(Title == "") |>
    select(year, 
           period, 
           period_start, 
           period_end, 
           Title, 
           -half, 
           Runtime, 
           Views, 
           `Hours Viewed`, 
           `Release Date`,
           `Available Globally?`, 
           live_event)
    }

  NETFLIX_DATA <- load_netflix_data()

# Create a table showing estimated fractions of shows and movies viewed in each period.

# Runtime in each half of calendar year was divided by 26 weeks to find whether the result was more than four          hours per week, likely indicating the title was a show. Furthermore, any title with "Season" was counted as a show.     
Show <- NETFLIX_DATA1|>
  filter(runtime/26 > 4 | str_detect(title, "Season"))|>
  group_by(period)|>
  summarize(total_shows = length(unique(title)),
            show_hoursviewed = sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE))

# Titles with less than or equal to four hours of runtime in every week of half calendar year, but excluding those     with "Season," likely indicates the title was a movie.

Movie <- NETFLIX_DATA1|>
  filter(runtime/26 <= 4 | is.na(runtime))|>
  filter_out(str_detect(title, "Season"))|>
  group_by(period)|>
  summarize(total_movies = length(unique(title)),
            movie_hoursviewed = sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE))

# For each period, the total of hours viewed with the percentages of views for shows and movies were calculated. 

Timespent <- Show|>
  inner_join(Movie, by = "period")|>
  mutate(total_hoursviewed = show_hoursviewed + movie_hoursviewed,
            percent_shows_hoursviewed = percent(show_hoursviewed/total_hoursviewed, accuracy = 0.01),
            percent_movies_hoursviewed = percent(movie_hoursviewed/total_hoursviewed, accuracy = 0.01))|>
  select(-total_hoursviewed)

gt(Timespent)|>
     tab_header(title = "Estimated Fractions Spent on Watching Shows and Movies",
                subtitle = "2023H1 to 2026H1")

# Create a table comparing the average viewership of live events and pre-taped contents in each period. The total of   viewership in each period was used to calculate the averages. The count of live events and pre-taped contents in     each period was included.

Live <- NETFLIX_DATA1 |>

  group_by(period)|>
  summarize(live_event_titles = length(unique(title)),
            live_event_views = sum(views, na.rm = TRUE))

Tape <- NETFLIX_DATA1 |>
  filter(live_event == "FALSE")|>
  group_by(period)|>
  summarize(taped_content_titles = length(unique(title)),
            taped_content_views = sum(views, na.rm = TRUE))

Viewspent <- Tape|>
  full_join(Live, by = "period")|>
  mutate(totalviews = taped_content_views + live_event_views,
         avg.views_taped_contents = percent(taped_content_views/totalviews, accuracy = 0.01),
         avg.views_live_event = percent(live_event_views/totalviews, accuracy = 0.01))|>
  select(-totalviews)

Title: Netflix Corporate Strategy Memo for 2027
To: Management
From: Katherine Mun
Date: October 16, 2026

Executive Summary
The number of views and view hours for 24,427 titles that ran in a half calendar year, between  2023-01-01 and 2026-06-30, were analyzed to plan releases in 2027.
Findings of Analysis
Between second half of 2024 and first half of 2026, around 98% or 99% of the total views came from pre-taped contents in each six months because of a high number of pre-taped contents. Approximately 7,000 and 8,000 were pre-taped contents, while less than 120 were live events.

Among the pre-taped contents, approximately 71% of shows and 29% of movies were viewed in the first half of 2023. However, since the second half of 2023, approximately 97% to 99% of shows were viewed because of a high number of shows. Approximately 6,000 to 7,500 were shows, while the number of movies has decreased from approximately 11,000 to below 700.
Recommendation
Based on the analysis, Netflix should continue to run a high number of pre-taped shows in 2027 to increase viewership.

title: Netflix
text:
#  This function will acquire and standardize all data of "What We Watched Reports"
#  from Netflix. Because Netflix hosts the data files behind a CDN, we
#  are accessing the release pages and automatically extracting links to the
#  relevant files (with CDN hash). 
# 
#  After import, files are stacked vertically and some basic cleaning is
#  performed. 
load_netflix_data <- function(){
  
  library(tidyverse)
  library(rvest)
  library(readxl)
  library(fs)
  library(scales)
  library(gt)

  
  data_dir <- path("data", "mp01")
    
  if(!dir_exists(data_dir)){
    dir_create(data_dir, showWarnings=FALSE, recurse=TRUE)
  }
  
  NETFLIX_URLS <- list(
    `2023H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-a-netflix-engagement-report",
    `2023H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2023",
    `2024H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2024",
    `2024H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2024",
    `2025H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2025",
    `2025H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2025",
    `2026H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2026"
  )
  
  download_if_needed <- function(url, local){
    if(!file_exists(local)){
      download.file(url, local, quiet = TRUE, mode = "wb")
    }
    
    return(local)
  }
    
  NETFLIX_URLS |> 
    map(read_html) |> 
    map(html_element, xpath = "//a[contains(@href, '.xlsx')]") |> 
    map_chr(html_attr, "href") |> 
    enframe("period", "url") |> 
   mutate(path = path(data_dir, paste0(period, ".xlsx")), 
          path = map2(url, path, download_if_needed), 
          data = map(path, read_excel, skip=3, na="*"), 
          data = map(data, \(x) x |> mutate(`Release Date` = as.Date(`Release Date`)))) |>
    unnest(data) |> 
    select(-url, -path) |> 
    mutate(year=str_sub(period, 1, 4), 
           half=str_sub(period, start=6), 
           period_start = make_date(year, if_else(half==1, 1, 7), 1), 
           period_end = make_date(year, if_else(half==1, 6, 12), if_else(half==1, 30, 31))) |> 
    filter(!is.na(`Hours Viewed`)) |> 
    mutate(live_event = !is.na(Runtime) & str_detect(Runtime, "\\d+:\\d+\\*"), 
           clean_time = str_remove(Runtime, fixed("*")),
           Runtime = 60 * hour(hm(clean_time)) + minute(hm(clean_time))) |>
    select(-clean_time) |>
    mutate(Runtime = coalesce(Runtime, mean(Runtime, na.rm=TRUE)), 
           .by=Title, 
           Title = stringi::stri_trans_general(Title, "Latin-ASCII"),
           Title = str_remove(Title, " // .*"), 
           Title = str_remove(Title, "[^[:ascii:]].*"), 
           Title = str_trim(Title)) |>
    filter_out(Title == "") |>
    select(year, 
           period, 
           period_start, 
           period_end, 
           Title, 
           -half, 
           Runtime, 
           Views, 
           `Hours Viewed`, 
           `Release Date`,
           `Available Globally?`, 
           live_event)
    }

  NETFLIX_DATA <- load_netflix_data()

# Create a table listing top titles by the number of views and fraction of hours viewed for each period. The total of   views in each period was used to show the top title's percentage of views. 

Top_Title <- NETFLIX_DATA1 |>
  group_by(period) |>
  summarize(totalviews = sum(views, na.rm = TRUE),
            highest_viewhours = max(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE))

Top_Title1 <- NETFLIX_DATA1 |>
  select(period, title, hours_viewed, views) |>
  inner_join(Top_Title, by = c("hours_viewed" = "highest_viewhours"))|>
  select(-period.y)|>
  rename(period = period.x)|>
  mutate(percent_views = percent(hours_viewed/totalviews))
 
  library(gt)
  gt(Top_Title1)|>
             tab_header(title = "Mostly Watched Seven Titles", 
                        subtitle = "in Each Half of Calendar Year")

# Create a table showing the titles with most consistently high viewership across all periods. To find the titles      appearing in all periods, the number of counts equaling seven was filtered. 

Viewership <- NETFLIX_DATA1 |>
  count(title)|>
  filter(n == 7)

# For each titles appearing in all seven periods, the total of views with the standard deviation, average, and the     minimum were calculated. The results were sorted by ascending order of standard deviation and descending order of    average views to show the most consistently viewed titles. 

Viewership1 <- NETFLIX_DATA1 |>
  select(title, views) |>
  inner_join(Viewership, by = c("title" = "title"))|>
  group_by(title) |>
  summarize(totalviews = sum(views, na.rm = TRUE),
            std_dev_views = sd(views, na.rm = TRUE),
            avg_views = mean(views, na.rm = TRUE),
            minimum_views = min(views, na.rm = FALSE))|>
  arrange(desc(avg_views), na.rm = FALSE)|>
  arrange(std_dev_views, na.rm = FALSE)              
  
gt(Viewership1)|>
  tab_header(title = "Most Consistently Viewed Titles in Every Seven Months, 2023H1 to 2026H1",  
             subtitle = "by ascending order of standard deviation and descending order 
                         of average of views")

# Create a table showing estimated fractions of shows and movies viewed in each period.

# Runtime in each half of calendar year was divided by 26 weeks to find whether the result was more than four          hours per week, likely indicating the title was a show. Furthermore, any title with "Season" was counted as a show.     
Show <- NETFLIX_DATA1|>
  filter(runtime/26 > 4 | str_detect(title, "Season"))|>
  group_by(period)|>
  summarize(total_shows = length(unique(title)),
            show_hoursviewed = sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE))

# Titles with less than or equal to four hours of runtime in every week of half calendar year, but excluding those     with "Season," likely indicates the title was a movie.

Movie <- NETFLIX_DATA1|>
  filter(runtime/26 <= 4 | is.na(runtime))|>
  filter_out(str_detect(title, "Season"))|>
  group_by(period)|>
  summarize(total_movies = length(unique(title)),
            movie_hoursviewed = sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE))

# For each period, the total of hours viewed with the percentages of views for shows and movies were calculated. 

Timespent <- Show|>
  inner_join(Movie, by = "period")|>
  mutate(total_hoursviewed = show_hoursviewed + movie_hoursviewed,
            percent_shows_hoursviewed = percent(show_hoursviewed/total_hoursviewed, accuracy = 0.01),
            percent_movies_hoursviewed = percent(movie_hoursviewed/total_hoursviewed, accuracy = 0.01))|>
  select(-total_hoursviewed)

gt(Timespent)|>
     tab_header(title = "Estimated Fractions Spent on Watching Shows and Movies",
                subtitle = "2023H1 to 2026H1")

# Create a table comparing the average viewership of live events and pre-taped contents in each period. The total of   viewership in each period was used to calculate the averages. The count of live events and pre-taped contents in     each period was included.

Live <- NETFLIX_DATA1 |>
  filter(live_event == "TRUE")|>
  group_by(period)|>
  summarize(live_event_titles = length(unique(title)),
            live_event_views = sum(views, na.rm = TRUE))

Tape <- NETFLIX_DATA1 |>
  filter(live_event == "FALSE")|>
  group_by(period)|>
  summarize(taped_content_titles = length(unique(title)),
            taped_content_views = sum(views, na.rm = TRUE))

Viewspent <- Tape|>
  full_join(Live, by = "period")|>
  mutate(totalviews = taped_content_views + live_event_views,
         avg.views_taped_contents = percent(taped_content_views/totalviews, accuracy = 0.01),
         avg.views_live_event = percent(live_event_views/totalviews, accuracy = 0.01))|>
  select(-totalviews)

gt(Viewspent)|>
     tab_header(title = "Average of Viewership on Live Events and Pre-taped Contents in Each Period",  
                subtitle = "2023H1 to 2026H1")

Title: Netflix Corporate Strategy Memo for 2027
To: Management
From: Katherine Mun
Date: October 16, 2026

Executive Summary
The number of views and view hours for 24,427 titles that ran in a half calendar year, between  2023-01-01 and 2026-06-30, were analyzed to plan releases in 2027.
Findings of Analysis
Between second half of 2024 and first half of 2026, around 98% or 99% of the total views came from pre-taped contents in each six months because of a high number of pre-taped contents. Approximately 7,000 and 8,000 were pre-taped contents, while less than 120 were live events.

Among the pre-taped contents, approximately 71% of shows and 29% of movies were viewed in the first half of 2023. However, since the second half of 2023, approximately 97% to 99% of shows were viewed because of a high number of shows. Approximately 6,000 to 7,500 were shows, while the number of movies has decreased from approximately 11,000 to below 700.
Recommendation
Based on the analysis, Netflix should continue to run a high number of pre-taped shows in 2027 to increase viewership.
